questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: The sugarcane that we use to make sugar and jaggery is the ______ of the plant.
questions.explanation: Sugarcane is the stem of the sugarcane plant, and sugar is made from its juice.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which of the following is a cereal?
questions.explanation: Rice, wheat and maize are cereals. Moong is a pulse, and groundnut and mustard are oilseeds.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which of these vegetables is an underground stem and not a root?
questions.explanation: A potato is a swollen underground stem. Carrot, radish and beetroot are roots.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which of these is a flower that we eat as a vegetable?
questions.explanation: Cauliflower is made of flower buds that we eat.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Why would a person who eats only honey for many weeks fall ill?
options: Honey lacks many nutrients such as proteins, vitamins and minerals in needed amounts
questions.explanation: Honey is mostly sugar, so a diet of only honey does not supply all nutrients.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Name three animals that give us food and write the food each one gives.
questions.answer: A cow gives milk, a hen gives eggs and a honeybee gives honey.
keyPoints: The correct food product for each
questions.explanation: Many foods come from animals, such as milk, eggs, honey and meat.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Explain why even a carnivore such as a lion depends indirectly on plants.
questions.answer: A lion eats animals such as deer, and the deer eat plants. If the plants were not there, the deer would have no food and the lion would have nothing to eat.
keyPoints: So the lion depends on plants indirectly
questions.explanation: Plants are the starting point of food for all living things.

questions.q: Which nutrients mainly give us energy?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates and fats are the main energy-giving nutrients.

questions.q: Lack of vitamin C causes a disease in which the gums bleed. It is called
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by lack of vitamin C, which is found in lemon, orange and amla.

questions.q: Difficulty in seeing in dim light is a sign of lack of
questions.explanation: Lack of vitamin A can cause night blindness.

questions.q: A girl feels weak and tired and her blood has less haemoglobin. Which mineral is she most likely lacking?
questions.explanation: Lack of iron causes anaemia.

questions.q: Sailors on long sea voyages in old times often had bleeding gums. Which food would best have prevented this?
questions.explanation: Citrus fruits provide vitamin C, which prevents scurvy.

questions.q: Name two functions of fats in the body and two food sources.
questions.answer: Fats give energy and keep the body warm. Sources are butter, ghee, oils and nuts.
questions.explanation: Fats provide more energy than the same amount of carbohydrates.

questions.q: Why should vegetables be washed before cutting and not overcooked?
questions.answer: Washing after cutting and overcooking can destroy or wash out vitamins and minerals, so food loses nutritive value.
questions.explanation: Careful cooking preserves nutrients.

questions.q: Which of these animals gives us wool?
questions.explanation: Sheep are the main source of wool.

questions.q: The machine used to weave cloth is called a
questions.explanation: Cloth is woven on a loom, either handloom or power loom.

questions.q: Cotton plants grow best in
options: Black soil in a warm climate
questions.explanation: Cotton needs warm weather and well-drained black soil.

questions.q: The rearing of silkworms for silk is called
questions.explanation: Sericulture is the rearing of silkworms to get silk.

questions.q: A sweater is made from a single long yarn using two needles. This process is
questions.explanation: Knitting uses a single yarn to make fabric, while weaving uses two sets of yarns at right angles.

questions.q: Name two natural fibres from plants and two from animals.
questions.answer: Plant fibres: cotton and jute. Animal fibres: wool and silk.
questions.explanation: Natural fibres come from plants and animals.

questions.q: Give one use of jute and explain why the jute fibre is suitable for it.
questions.answer: Jute is used to make gunny bags and ropes because the fibre is strong and coarse.
questions.explanation: The properties of a fibre decide its use.

questions.q: Which of these is opaque?
questions.explanation: A brick does not allow light to pass.

questions.q: Which of these materials is hard?
questions.explanation: Iron cannot be easily compressed or scratched.

questions.q: Which of the following is lustrous?
questions.explanation: Metals like gold have a shiny surface.

questions.q: All the substances in which group mix completely with water?
questions.explanation: Sugar and salt dissolve, and vinegar mixes with water.

questions.q: Cooking vessels are made of metals such as steel and aluminium. Which is the best reason?
options: Metals let heat pass easily to the food
questions.explanation: Metals are good conductors of heat.

questions.q: Why do we group materials? Give two properties used for grouping.
questions.answer: Grouping makes it easier to study and use them. We can group them by appearance, hardness, solubility, or whether they float or sink.
questions.explanation: Materials with similar properties are placed together.

questions.q: Describe a simple activity to find out if a material is soluble in water.
questions.answer: Add a spoonful of the material to a glass of water and stir well. If it disappears and the water looks uniform, it is soluble. If it stays as separate particles, it is insoluble.
questions.explanation: A fair test uses the same amount of water for each material.

questions.q: Separating insoluble solids from liquid with filter paper is called
questions.explanation: The liquid passes through the filter paper and the solids stay on it.

questions.q: Stones are picked out of rice by
questions.explanation: Handpicking works when the quantity is small and the pieces can be seen.

questions.q: A solution in which no more of a substance can dissolve at a given temperature is
questions.explanation: That is a saturated solution.

questions.q: When water vapour is cooled and changes to liquid water, the process is called
questions.explanation: Cooling turns vapour into liquid, which is condensation.

questions.q: A muddy water sample is to be made clear. Which order of steps is most suitable?
options: Let it stand, pour off clear water, then filter
questions.explanation: Sedimentation and decantation remove most mud, and filtration removes the remaining fine particles.

questions.q: What is evaporation? Give one use of it.
questions.answer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour. It is used to get salt from sea water or to dry wet clothes.
questions.explanation: Evaporation leaves dissolved solids behind.

questions.q: A mixture contains chalk powder, iron filings and salt. Describe how to separate all three.
questions.answer: Use a magnet to remove the iron filings. Add water so salt dissolves and filter to remove chalk. Evaporate the filtrate to get salt.
questions.explanation: Choose each method according to the property of the substance.

questions.q: The change from solid ice to liquid water is called
questions.explanation: A solid changing to a liquid on heating is melting.

questions.q: Which of the following is a change of state from liquid to gas?
questions.explanation: Evaporation or boiling changes a liquid into vapour.

questions.q: Baking soda is added to vinegar and bubbles appear. Why is it said to be an irreversible change?
options: New substances are formed and cannot be turned back easily
questions.explanation: A gas is produced and new substances form, so the original ones are not recovered easily.

questions.q: Which of these changes can be reversed?
questions.explanation: Salt can be recovered by evaporating the water.

questions.q: A small gap is left between the rails of a railway track. Why?
options: Iron expands in summer and would bend the track without the gap
questions.explanation: Metals expand on heating, so gaps allow room for expansion.

questions.q: Why is the making of curd from milk considered an irreversible change?
questions.answer: Curd has different properties from milk and the curd cannot be changed back into milk.
questions.explanation: A change in which a new substance forms permanently is irreversible.

questions.q: A burning candle shows both reversible and irreversible changes. Explain.
questions.answer: Wax that melts near the flame and solidifies on cooling is a reversible change. The wax that burns gives new substances and cannot be recovered, which is irreversible.
questions.explanation: One event may include both types of change.

questions.q: Plants with weak stems that climb up with the help of support are called
questions.explanation: Climbers, like the pea plant, wind around supports.

questions.q: The part of the plant that makes seeds and fruits is the
questions.explanation: The flower is the reproductive part of a plant.

questions.q: Which gas do leaves take in from air for making food?
questions.explanation: Leaves take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen during photosynthesis.

questions.q: After pollination and fertilisation, the ovary of the flower develops into a
questions.explanation: The ovary develops into a fruit, and the ovules into seeds.

questions.q: If all the leaves of a plant are removed and the plant is kept in the sun, what happens?
options: It makes much less food, since leaves are the main food-making parts
questions.explanation: Leaves have chlorophyll and make food using sunlight.

questions.q: Give two differences between tap root and fibrous root with one example of each.
questions.answer: A tap root has one main root with side branches (mango, gram). A fibrous root is a cluster of roots of similar size (wheat, grass).
questions.explanation: Root type is related to leaf venation.

questions.q: Explain photosynthesis, mentioning raw materials and products.
questions.answer: In photosynthesis the leaf uses carbon dioxide and water, with sunlight and chlorophyll, to make food (starch/glucose) and release oxygen.
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis happens in green parts of the plant.

questions.q: The backbone protects the
questions.explanation: The vertebral column surrounds and protects the spinal cord.

questions.q: A joint that does not allow any movement is a
questions.explanation: Fixed joints, like those of the skull, allow no movement.

questions.q: The joint between the skull and the top of the backbone, which allows us to nod and turn the head, is called a
questions.explanation: A pivotal joint in the neck allows the head to turn.

questions.q: A fish moves forward in water mainly with the help of its
questions.explanation: Its body shape reduces resistance, and fins and tail help it swim.

questions.q: An earthworm has no bones yet can crawl. What helps it to move?
options: Muscles and tiny bristles that grip the ground
questions.explanation: Alternating contraction and relaxation of muscles and bristles help it to crawl.

questions.q: List three features that help a bird to fly.
questions.answer: Birds have light, hollow bones, strong chest muscles to flap the wings, and a streamlined body with feathers.
questions.explanation: Birds' bodies are suited to flight.

questions.q: Compare the way a snake and a fish move.
questions.answer: A snake moves by making curves in the body and pushing against the ground using muscles and ribs. A fish pushes through water using its tail and fins with a streamlined body.
keyPoints: Fish uses tail and fins in water
questions.explanation: The surrounding decides the way of moving.

questions.q: A pond is an example of an
questions.explanation: Habitats in water are aquatic habitats.

questions.q: Which of the following is an abiotic part of a habitat?
questions.explanation: Air is a non-living component.

questions.q: Which animal is well adapted for living in the desert?
questions.explanation: A camel has long legs, a hump that stores fat and thick eyelashes, which suit desert life.

questions.q: The webbed feet of a duck help it to
questions.explanation: Webbed feet push against water to help the duck swim.

questions.q: A fish taken out of water dies soon because
options: Its gills cannot take oxygen from air as they do from water
questions.explanation: Gills are adapted to take dissolved oxygen from water.

questions.q: Differentiate between terrestrial and aquatic habitats with one example each.
questions.answer: Terrestrial habitats are on land, such as forests and deserts. Aquatic habitats are in water, such as ponds and oceans.
questions.explanation: Habitats are broadly grouped as land or water.

questions.q: A potted seedling placed near a window bends toward the light. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
questions.answer: It shows that living things respond to stimuli, here light, by changing the direction of growth.
questions.explanation: Plants respond to light, although they do not move from place to place.

questions.q: One metre is equal to
Which of these is used to measure the length of a cloth?
questions.explanation: A measuring tape or metre scale measures length.

questions.q: A stone tied to a string and whirled around in a circle shows
options: Rotational motion of the stone only
questions.explanation: The stone follows a circular path.

questions.q: Which of these is not a standard unit of length?
questions.explanation: A cubit was an old unit based on the forearm and varies between people.

questions.q: A bicycle moves along a straight road while its wheels turn. Which statement is correct?
options: The cycle shows rectilinear motion and the wheels show rotational motion
questions.explanation: A body can show more than one type of motion at once.

questions.q: Give three examples of periodic motion.
questions.answer: The swing of a pendulum, the to-and-fro motion of a swing and the motion of the Earth around the Sun.
questions.explanation: Periodic motion repeats itself at regular intervals.

questions.q: The end of a ruler is broken and you must start from the 2 cm mark. How would you find the length of a pencil that ends at 11 cm?
questions.answer: Subtract the starting reading from the final reading: 11 cm minus 2 cm gives 9 cm.
keyPoints: Do not start at the damaged end
Subtract the first reading from the last
questions.explanation: Length is the difference between two readings.

questions.q: Which of these is a luminous object?
questions.explanation: The Sun gives off its own light.

questions.q: Which of these is non-luminous?
questions.explanation: A tree does not emit light of its own.

questions.q: The shadow of a sheet of butter paper held in front of a torch will be
questions.explanation: Translucent material lets some light pass, so its shadow is faint.

questions.q: If you raise your right hand in front of a plane mirror, the image seems to raise the
questions.explanation: A plane mirror reverses left and right, which is lateral inversion.

questions.q: Shadows are long in early morning and late evening. The reason is
options: The Sun is low in the sky
questions.explanation: When the Sun is low, light falls at a slant and shadows stretch longer.

questions.q: Name three uses of mirrors in daily life.
questions.answer: Mirrors are used in dressing tables, as rear-view mirrors in vehicles and in barber shops.
questions.explanation: Mirrors reflect light to give images.

questions.q: Why does a clear glass sheet held before a torch form hardly any shadow?
questions.answer: Clear glass is transparent so almost all light passes through, and very little light is blocked.
keyPoints: Little light blocked so no dark shadow
questions.explanation: A shadow forms only where light is blocked.

questions.q: A cell has how many terminals?
questions.explanation: A cell has a positive and a negative terminal.

questions.q: Which of these is an electrical insulator?
questions.explanation: Plastic does not conduct electricity.

questions.q: In an electric circuit with the switch open, the bulb
questions.explanation: An open switch breaks the circuit so no current flows.

questions.q: In an LED, the longer lead is connected to the
questions.explanation: The longer lead of an LED is its positive terminal.

questions.q: A student connects a bulb, a cell, a switch and wires correctly in a closed loop but the bulb does not glow. What is the likely fault?
options: The filament of the bulb is broken (fused)
questions.explanation: A broken filament leaves a gap in the circuit so current cannot flow.

questions.q: Differentiate a conductor from an insulator with two examples of each.
questions.answer: Conductors allow electricity to pass, such as copper and iron. Insulators do not, such as rubber and plastic.
questions.explanation: Metals are generally conductors.

questions.q: Why do electricians use tools with rubber or plastic handles?
questions.answer: Rubber and plastic are insulators, so they stop current from flowing through the tool to the electrician, which protects against shocks.
questions.explanation: Insulation provides safety.

questions.q: A naturally occurring magnet is called
questions.explanation: Lodestone (magnetite) is a natural magnet.

questions.q: The attracting power of a bar magnet is strongest at its
questions.explanation: Iron filings cling mostly near the ends, which are the poles.

questions.q: If the north pole of one magnet is brought near the south pole of another magnet, they will
questions.explanation: Unlike poles attract.

questions.q: Which of the following is not attracted by a magnet?
questions.explanation: Aluminium is a non-magnetic material.

questions.q: Why does a magnet get weaker if it is heated or hammered?
options: Its tiny magnetic parts get disordered
questions.explanation: Heating and hammering disturb the arrangement of the tiny magnetic regions.

questions.q: Give two uses of magnets in everyday life.
questions.answer: Magnets are used in compass needles, refrigerator door seals and magnetic toys.
questions.explanation: Magnets are found in many household devices.

questions.q: How can an iron needle be made into a magnet by stroking?
questions.answer: Stroke the needle many times from one end to the other in the same direction with one pole of a bar magnet, lifting the magnet away at the end of each stroke. Then test it on pins.
questions.explanation: Stroking lines up the tiny magnetic parts of the needle.
